status: concepts awaiting owner selection; not a rig or animation compatibility test
brief: Owner rejected all 2026-09-26 concepts: too many tiny details and too small anchor. Two new designs for the smoke-and-light HUD direction, preserving existing Pelag body proportions, joint placement and garment clearances for reusing animations.

variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a polished new character-design presentation for Pelag, playable hero of The War Remains, redesigned to belong with the game's new painterly ink/smoke/fire HUD.
References: Image 1 is the EXISTING hero: strictly preserve recognizable face, dark swept hair, red headband, skin tone, body proportions, height, limb lengths, shoulder width, hand size, joint positions and foot profile. His existing human combat animation skeleton must remain reusable. Image 2 is the APPROVED HUD art direction: painterly charcoal/blue-black shadows, warm ivory light, restrained ember/coral accents, expressive broad brush shapes. Translate its visual language into wearable costume and painted materials, not actual smoke replacing anatomy. Image 3 is the existing approved anchor design: preserve the smooth substantial flukes, diamond centre, metal ring, real heavy chain and separate handheld loop grip.
Composition: landscape character concept sheet, one design only. Large full-body front A-pose on left, same full-body rear three-quarter A-pose at middle-right, small three-quarter game-camera silhouette inset at far right. All views must match precisely. Grounded heavy anchor clearly shown beside the front figure for scale, and its sensible diagonal back carry shown on rear view. Sparse clean composition, warm grey paper backdrop with faint charcoal edge wash, beautiful painterly premium ARPG rendering, crisp and sculptural, never toy-plastic. The front A-pose has free hands for judging rig compatibility.
Anchor: very noticeably larger than a belt trinket, approximately 0.9 metres high for a 1.78m hero and 0.6m across flukes, dense blackened silver metal with broad ivory edge highlights; the weapon's mass is a defining part of his silhouette. Keep existing weapon architecture and separate sockets, no fused chain/body. In back carry it remains within a workable torso/hip diagonal envelope and clear of legs.
Costume: 3 or 4 strong masses, broad readable folds, clean intentional shapes. Fewer larger details, very limited fittings, no visual clutter. Cloth stays within existing upper-thigh-length split garment envelope, knee-length trousers. Keep shoulders/elbows/knees free. Thin flexible surfaces over the existing silhouette, no bulky armour requiring new animations, no cape, floor-length coat, skirt bridging the legs, extra limbs, massive shoulder pads, huge boots, weaponized oversized hands or new body proportions.
Avoid patchwork, patches, tiny stitches, rivet noise, many belts, necklaces, trinkets, repeated ornaments, ragged little cloth scraps, embroidery, gold filigree, photoreal leather pores, neon trim, glowing anatomy, flames around the entire body. No HUD redesign, no logo, no captions except a tiny option number. This is a distinct mature art direction with simplified beautiful design, NOT the rejected busy patchwork pirate sheet.
OPTION 01: Dark charcoal/navy cropped open sailor's jacket with clean angular lapels and sleeves ending just above elbows; a single broad warm ivory undershirt plane opens the chest and is visible below the waist. Burnt-coral headband and ONE broad coral waist sash, small controlled tails above mid-thigh. Dark knee-length trousers and low simple brown open footwear matching the reference ankle/sole shape. Simple smooth wrist wraps. One broad functional diagonal anchor harness, minimal dull silver fastening. Asymmetric ivory shirt hem makes a bold pale diagonal from chest to hip. Blackened silver anchor, cool silver saber in a plain scabbard at the original hip position. Strong adventurous confident young hero, readable warm face, broad brush-lit planes. Contrast dominated by dark torso and ivory light, restrained ember coral. Tiny label '01'.
